name: M-26-14 DM: Data Retirement — Gate 1 Approval Pending
description: Detects M-26-14 managed indices awaiting Gate 1 (pre-retirement) approval in the two-gate data retirement chain. Fires when the newest pending_gate1 record for an index is more than 24 hours old and no approved_gate1 or cancelled record for the same index is newer than it (latest-record semantics: the ledger is append-only, so a cancellation older than a fresh re-proposal no longer masks it). The 90-day lookback (on event.ingested, stamped by the ledger pipeline) covers the realistic pending horizon; a request pending longer than that is itself a process failure and should be caught by periodic manual audit of m_26_14-retirement-requests.
author: Elastic
query: FROM m_26_14-retirement-requests | WHERE index_name IS NOT NULL AND state IN ("pending_gate1", "approved_gate1", "cancelled") | EVAL ts = COALESCE(updated_at, created_at, @timestamp) | STATS pending_created = MAX(CASE(state == "pending_gate1", COALESCE(created_at, ts), NULL)), last_resolution = MAX(CASE(state IN ("approved_gate1", "cancelled"), ts, NULL)), last_updated = MAX(ts), ilm_policies = VALUES(ilm_policy), request_ids = VALUES(request_id) BY index_name | WHERE pending_created IS NOT NULL AND (last_resolution IS NULL OR last_resolution < pending_created) AND DATE_DIFF("hours", pending_created, NOW()) > 24 | EVAL pending_hours = DATE_DIFF("hours", pending_created, NOW()) | SORT pending_created ASC
note:
## Triage and Investigation

### Step 1 — Review the retirement candidates
- Query `m_26_14-retirement-requests` for the newest record per index (`state: pending_gate1`) to see all open candidates; the alert carries `request_ids` and `pending_hours`.
- For each candidate index confirm: lifecycle age against `retention_days`, ILM policy, business owner, and whether any active legal hold applies.

### Step 2 — Check for legal holds or investigations
- Review `m_26_14-retirement-requests` for `legal_hold_initiated` records whose `source_index` names the same data stream or matches the backing index (ILM mount prefixes `partial-`/`restored-` do not count).
- Consult legal/compliance for ongoing investigations.

### Step 3 — Approve or cancel (one NEW record; the ledger is append-only)
- To **approve Gate 1**: `POST m_26_14-retirement-requests/_doc {"request_id": "<index>-gate1-<now-iso>", "index_name": "<name exactly as listed>", "state": "approved_gate1", "gate1_approved_by": "<your-username>", "gate1_approved_at": "<now-iso>"}`
- To **cancel retirement**: `POST m_26_14-retirement-requests/_doc {"request_id": "<index>-cancel-<now-iso>", "index_name": "<name>", "state": "cancelled", "cancelled_by": "<username>", "cancelled_at": "<now-iso>", "notes": "<why>"}`
- The ledger pipeline stamps `@timestamp`, `updated_at` and `event.ingested`. Approval is picked up by the Gate 1 approval watcher (`m_26_14-gate1-approval-advance`) within the hour, which writes `pending_gate2` and opens the Gate 2 Case. **No ILM change happens at Gate 1**; the index stays on its no-delete policy until a second person approves Gate 2.

### Step 4 — Verify in Kibana Cases
- Find the associated Gate 1 case in Security > Cases and update it with your decision.
- The two-gate audit trail is `m_26_14-retirement-requests`; runbook `docs/runbooks/data-retirement.md`.

### Latest-record semantics
This rule groups ledger records by `index_name` and alerts only when the newest `pending_gate1` record has no newer `approved_gate1` or `cancelled` record. Approvals and cancellations are new documents, never edits of the pending record.
setup:
### Supersession semantics
This rule groups all workflow records by `index_name` and alerts only when a pending record exists with no superseding state for the same index. Approvals and cancellations indexed as new documents (per the approval instructions above) therefore clear the alert condition without needing to update the original pending document in place.
